Win Big's prizes make it a game with most of its money in small, frequent prizes. Of the prize money still unclaimed, about three-quarters is in wins under $5,000. The prize counts change every day, but this design does not.

Every line of Win Big's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
951.headline: How the prize money is divided

952.body:
Of the unclaimed prize money on "Millionaire Bucks", most is in wins under $2,000. The game is a game built around small prizes that are won often. That is neither good nor bad, only how it was designed. Choose the kind of game that fits the win you want.

The table below shows the full count for "Millionaire Bucks", with every prize level included.
952.headline: What type of game it is

959.body:
"LOTERIA®" has had no $75,000 top prize claimed since we started watching it. Everyday prizes keep getting claimed, and fewer tickets are left each day. The number of tickets printed is fixed. Each day without a top prize claim leaves those prizes among fewer tickets.

Tomorrow's count on "LOTERIA®" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
959.headline: Six months, no top prize claimed

972.body:
"$8 Million Money Maker" is in the second half of its run, with about a quarter of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, the top prizes and the tickets are going at about the same pace.

One of $8 Million Money Maker's five top prizes can still be won.

Today's free summary of "$8 Million Money Maker" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
972.headline: Tickets sold so far

975.body:
"$1,000,000 Money Rush" offers a top prize of $1 million and eleven prize levels in all. The prize money leans toward many smaller prizes. Games shaped like this give out wins often, but rarely large ones. This design never changes, while every other number on this page does.

The numbers for "$1,000,000 Money Rush" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
975.headline: The prize mix in this game

976.body:
"100X The Cash" paid out its last $2 million prize over a month ago. The ticket still advertises it because printed tickets never change. Prize tables do change, and the biggest prize listed today is $10,000.

If you play "100X The Cash" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
976.headline: No $2 million prize is left

980.body:
"20X The Cash" has 276,353 prizes of $5 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $10,000 prize, with four left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

The numbers for "20X The Cash" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
980.headline: Prize table details

981.body:
"50X The Cash" is close to selling out, with only a small slice of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, neither the tickets nor the top prizes are running out faster than the other.

If "50X The Cash" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
981.headline: How far along this game is

985.body:
About half of the tickets for "MAX-A-MILLION" are sold. The top prize count has held, with twelve of 25 still unclaimed. The number of tickets printed is fixed, so that is a plain good sign.

Everything here about "MAX-A-MILLION" comes from official North Carolina lottery numbers, current through November 7.

988.headline: Top prizes have lasted so far

990.body:
The most common win left on "LADY LUCK" is $2. The second biggest prize left is $1,000, and seven of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

Everything here about "LADY LUCK" comes from official North Carolina lottery numbers, current through November 7.
990.headline: What's actually left to win

992.body:
Of all the tickets printed for "$2 MILLION VAULT", about a quarter are still unsold. The game is in the second half of its run, with one of three top prizes unclaimed. In every scratcher, either the tickets or the prizes run out first. The rest of this page shows the details.

Everything above about "$2 MILLION VAULT" comes from the North Carolina Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
992.headline: Tickets sold so far

993.body:
The top prize count on "$5,000 Triple Play" has not moved for five months. The game still has three of six top prizes unclaimed. Smaller prizes keep getting claimed as tickets sell. The same top prizes are now among fewer tickets.

Tomorrow's count on "$5,000 Triple Play" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
993.headline: Good news: no big claims

994.body:
Of the unclaimed prize money on "$25,000 Triple Play", nearly all is in wins under $500. The game is a game with most of its money in small, frequent prizes. That is neither good nor bad, only how it was designed. Choose the kind of game that fits the win you want.

Right now, the top prizes are being claimed more slowly than the tickets are selling, which is a good sign.
